symbols.name: fail
symbols.def: \(\bot\) is the single failure value returned by every algebraic construction outside its declared domain.

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: The number \(\ell\) of latent confounders; the main frontier restricts to \(\ell\ge 1\).

symbols.name: J_ell
symbols.def: \(J_{\ell}=\{0,1,\ldots,\ell,t,y\}\) indexes the normalized proxy disturbance, latent sources, treatment disturbance, and outcome disturbance.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: \(L=(L_i)_{i\in I_{\ell}}\) is the latent-source family.

symbols.name: eps_Z
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_Z\) is the proxy disturbance.

symbols.name: eps_T
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_T\) is the treatment disturbance.

symbols.name: eps_Y
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_Y\) is the outcome disturbance.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: \(a=(a_i)_{i\in I_{\ell}}\) contains latent-to-proxy coefficients.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: \(b=(b_i)_{i\in I_{\ell}}\) contains latent-to-treatment coefficients.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: \(c=(c_i)_{i\in I_{\ell}}\) contains latent-to-outcome coefficients.

symbols.name: S_j
symbols.def: \(S_0=\varepsilon_Z\) and \(S_i=a_iL_i\) for \(i\in I_{\ell}\).

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: \(\gamma\) is the coefficient on the edge \(Z\to T\).

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: \(\beta\) is the coefficient on \(T\to Y\) and the causal target.

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: \(u_i=\gamma+b_i/a_i\).

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: \(v_i=\beta u_i+c_i/a_i\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: \(Z\) is the observed proxy.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T\) is the observed treatment.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(Y\) is the observed outcome.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X=(Z,T,Y)^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: \(P=\mathcal L(X)\) is the observed law.

symbols.name: M_ell
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{\ell}\) is the class of observed laws generated by the fixed proxy graph and the source conditions.

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R\) is the largest retained cumulant order.

symbols.name: K_R
symbols.def: \(K_R=\{0,\ldots,R\}\) indexes atoms in a finite presentation of each truncated source-moment sequence.

symbols.name: C_r
symbols.def: \(C_r=\operatorname{Cum}_r(X)\) for \(2\le r\le R\).

symbols.name: C_le_R
symbols.def: \(C_{\le R}=(C_2,\ldots,C_R)\).

symbols.name: m_src_R
symbols.def: \(m^{S}_{j,r}\) is the centered raw moment of order \(r\) assigned to source \(j\in J_{\ell}\), with \(m^{S}_{j,0}=1\) and \(m^{S}_{j,1}=0\).

symbols.name: w_src_R
symbols.def: \(w^{S}_{j,k}\) is the mass of atomic witness \(k\in K_R\) for source \(j\).

symbols.name: x_src_R
symbols.def: \(x^{S}_{j,k}\) is the location of atomic witness \(k\in K_R\) for source \(j\).

symbols.name: kappa_src_R
symbols.def: \(\kappa^{S}_{j,r}=\sum_{\pi\vdash\{1,\ldots,r\}}(|\pi|-1)!(-1)^{|\pi|-1}\prod_{B\in\pi}m^{S}_{j,|B|}\) is the univariate moment-to-cumulant polynomial.
symbols.role: source cumulants in the observable map

symbols.name: Theta_ell_R
symbols.def: \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\) is the semialgebraic set of normalized coordinates \(\theta=(\gamma,\beta,u,v,m^{S})\) satisfying \(\gamma\prod_{i\in I_{\ell}}(u_i-\gamma)(v_i-\beta u_i)\ne0\) and, for every \(j\in J_{\ell}\), admitting \(w^{S}_{j,k}\ge0,x^{S}_{j,k}\in\mathbb R\) indexed by \(k\in K_R\) with \(\sum_kw^{S}_{j,k}=1\), \(\sum_kw^{S}_{j,k}x^{S}_{j,k}=0\), \(m^{S}_{j,r}=\sum_kw^{S}_{j,k}(x^{S}_{j,k})^r\) for \(0\le r\le R\), and \(m^{S}_{j,2}>0\); the corresponding original graph chart is \(a_i=1,b_i=u_i-\gamma,c_i=v_i-\beta u_i\).

symbols.name: Phi_ell_R
symbols.def: \(\Phi_{\ell,R}\) is the polynomial map \(C_r=\kappa^{S}_{0,r}(1,\gamma,\beta\gamma)^{\otimes r}+\sum_{i\in I_{\ell}}\kappa^{S}_{i,r}(1,u_i,v_i)^{\otimes r}+\kappa^{S}_{t,r}(0,1,\beta)^{\otimes r}+\kappa^{S}_{y,r}(0,0,1)^{\otimes r}\) for \(2\le r\le R\), restricted to \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\).

symbols.name: O_ell_R
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}=\{\zeta:\exists\theta\in\Theta_{\ell,R},\ \Phi_{\ell,R}(\theta)=\zeta\}\) is the legal observable truncated-cumulant image, given by a finite quantified-real formula and hence semialgebraic.

symbols.name: F_ell_R
symbols.def: For \(\zeta\in\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), \(F_{\ell,R}(\zeta)=\{\theta\in\Theta_{\ell,R}:\Phi_{\ell,R}(\theta)=\zeta\}\).

symbols.name: r_beta
symbols.def: \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\) is the least \(R\) for which \(\beta\) is constant on every fiber over a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), and equals \(\bot\) if no such \(R\) exists.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: \(d\) is an annihilating-polynomial degree.

symbols.name: H_d
symbols.def: \(H_d=\mathbb R[x_z,x_t,x_y]_d\) is the space of homogeneous ternary forms of degree \(d\).

symbols.name: N_d
symbols.def: \(N_d=\dim H_d=\binom{d+2}{2}\).

symbols.name: p_j
symbols.def: After absorbing \(a_i\) into \(L_i\), \(p_0=(1,\gamma,\beta\gamma)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(p_i=(1,u_i,v_i)^{\mathsf T}\) for \(i\in I_{\ell}\).

symbols.name: q_beta
symbols.def: \(q_{\beta}=(0,1,\beta)^{\mathsf T}\) is the treatment-noise loading.

symbols.name: e_y
symbols.def: \(e_y=(0,0,1)^{\mathsf T}\) is the outcome-noise loading.

symbols.name: A_R_d
symbols.def: \((A_{R,d}f)_{m,\eta}=C_{d+m+1}[Z,f,X^{\eta}]\) for \(m\ge0\), \(|\eta|=m\), and \(d+m+1\le R\); when the index set is empty, the codomain is the zero space and \(A_{R,d}\) is the zero map.

symbols.name: E_d
symbols.def: \((E_df)_j=f(p_j)\) for \(0\le j\le\ell\).

symbols.name: B_R_d
symbols.def: \((B_{R,d})_{(m,\eta),j}=\operatorname{Cum}_{d+m+1}(S_j)p_j^{\eta}\) for the same row indices as \(A_{R,d}\), where \(S_0=\varepsilon_Z\) and \(S_i=a_iL_i\); it is the unique empty-row matrix when that index set is empty.

symbols.name: M_3
symbols.def: \((M_3)_{ab}=\operatorname{Cum}(Z,X_a,X_b)\).

symbols.name: Delta_R_d
symbols.def: For each explicitly supplied row-minor, kernel-pivot, and denominator record with \(1\le d\le R-2\), \(\Delta_{R,d}(C_{\le R})\) is their polynomial product on the entire cumulant-coordinate space; for an inadmissible record it is identically zero.

symbols.name: g_R_d
symbols.def: For an explicitly supplied chart record, \(g_{R,d}(C_{\le R})=C_{d+2}[f,T,Y]/C_{d+2}[f,T,T]\) when its recorded minor, pivot, and denominator are all nonzero, and \(g_{R,d}(C_{\le R})=\bot\) otherwise.

symbols.name: d_ell
symbols.def: \(d_{\ell}=\min\{d\ge1:\binom{d+2}{2}>\ell+1\}\); the set is nonempty because the binomial coefficient diverges with \(d\).

symbols.name: h_ell
symbols.def: \(h_{\ell}=\min\{h\ge1:\binom{h+3}{3}\ge\ell+1\}\); the set is nonempty because the binomial coefficient diverges with \(h\).

symbols.name: chi
symbols.def: \(\chi=(d,J,p,k)\) records an annihilator degree, a row-minor index, a kernel pivot, and a denominator candidate, ordered first by \(d\) and then lexicographically by \(J,p,k\).

symbols.name: d_chi
symbols.def: \(d_{\chi}\) is the annihilator degree recorded by chart \(\chi\).

symbols.name: Delta_chi
symbols.def: \(\Delta_{\chi}\) is the rank-minor, kernel-pivot, and contraction-denominator polynomial recorded by chart \(\chi\).

symbols.name: D_chi
symbols.def: \(\mathcal U_{\chi}=\{\zeta:\Delta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ne0\}\) is the exact nonvanishing domain of the chart constructions.

symbols.name: f_chi
symbols.def: \(f_{\chi}(\zeta)\in H_{d_{\chi}}\) is the row-reduced kernel vector for \(\zeta\in\mathcal U_{\chi}\), and \(f_{\chi}(\zeta)=\bot\) outside that domain.

symbols.name: g_chi
symbols.def: \(g_{\chi}(\zeta)\) is the recorded rational contraction ratio using \(f_{\chi}(\zeta)\) for \(\zeta\in\mathcal U_{\chi}\), and is \(\bot\) outside that domain.

symbols.name: A_id_ell_R
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,R}\) is the finite ordered set of chart records \(\chi\) for which \(\mathcal U_{\chi}\cap\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\ne\varnothing\) and \(g_{\chi}(\Phi_{\ell,R}(\theta))=\beta(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_{\ell,R}\) with \(\Phi_{\ell,R}(\theta)\in\mathcal U_{\chi}\); the set itself is total and may be empty.

symbols.name: k_ell
symbols.def: \(k(\ell)=(\ell+2)+\lceil(-3+\sqrt{8\ell+17})/2\rceil\) is the published sufficient cumulant order.

symbols.name: L_ell
symbols.def: \(L_{\ell}=\max\{3,\min\{R\ge2:\binom{R+2}{2}>\ell+3\}\}\); the inner set is nonempty because the binomial coefficient diverges with \(R\).

symbols.name: H_exact
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak H_{\ell}\) is the procedure that forms the two-representation incidence ideal for \(\Phi_{\ell,R}\), saturates graph and rank factors, projects to \((\beta,\beta')\), and certifies surviving real branches by finitely atomic truncated-moment constraints.

symbols.name: beta_prime
symbols.def: \(\beta'\) is the effect coordinate in a second structural representation of the same cumulant tuple.

symbols.name: J_1_3
symbols.def: \(J_{1,3}\) is the complete two-representation incidence ideal obtained from two copies of the order-three modified map \((\beta,\Phi_{1,3})\) with a common complete centered ternary cumulant tuple, before imposing real truncated-moment inequalities.

symbols.name: D_1_3
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_{1,3}\) is the complete algebraic image-closure scheme of the published modified map \((\beta,\Phi_{1,3})\) when the diagonal order-two and order-three source coordinates are treated as unrestricted real or complex scalars.

symbols.name: s_1_3
symbols.def: \(s_{1,3}\) is the product of the nonzero graph coefficients, the selected rank-two minor of \(M_3\), and the recovery contraction denominator in both representations.

symbols.name: G_1_3
symbols.def: \(G_{1,3}=(G_j)_j\) is an explicitly ordered generating list for \(J_{1,3}\).

symbols.name: R_1_3_legal
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R^{\mathrm{legal}}_{1,3}\) consists of the equations in \(G_{1,3}\), the atomic equations \(m^{S}_{j,r}=\sum_{k=0}^{3}w^{S}_{j,k}(x^{S}_{j,k})^r\), \(\sum_kw^{S}_{j,k}=1\), \(\sum_kw^{S}_{j,k}x^{S}_{j,k}=0\), and the inequalities \(w^{S}_{j,k}\ge0\), \(m^{S}_{j,2}>0\), together with the nonzero graph and saturation conditions, for both representations.

symbols.name: D_Psi3
symbols.def: \(\mathcal W_3\) is the finite semialgebraic set of rational chart coordinates on which every denominator of the displayed three-atom formulas is nonzero, every atom probability is strictly positive, every variance is positive, and every nonzero graph factor holds.
symbols.role: domain of the legal order-three realization

symbols.name: Psi_3
symbols.def: \(\Psi_3(t)\) is the displayed rational three-atom structural realization in \(\Theta_{1,3}\) for \(t\in\mathcal W_3\), and equals \(\bot\) for \(t\notin\mathcal W_3\).

symbols.name: D_Psi2
symbols.def: \(\mathcal W_2\) is the finite semialgebraic set of rational twin coordinates on which both displayed three-atom formulas have nonzero denominators, strictly positive atom probabilities and variances, and nonzero graph factors.
symbols.role: common domain of the legal covariance twins

symbols.name: Psi_2_pm
symbols.def: For \(t\in\mathcal W_2\), \(\Psi_2^{+}(t)\) and \(\Psi_2^{-}(t)\) are the displayed three-atom structural points in \(\Theta_{1,2}\); outside \(\mathcal W_2\), both maps return \(\bot\).

symbols.name: H_one
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak H_{1,3}\) reproduces the vanishing ideal of the complete modified order-three map, computes \(J_{1,3}:s_{1,3}^{\infty}\), factors its eliminated beta polynomial, and for the factor distinct from the observable contraction root computes an exact real-infeasibility certificate against \(\mathcal R^{\mathrm{legal}}_{1,3}\); it also produces \(\Psi_3,\Psi_2^{+},\Psi_2^{-}\) with exact rational atoms and weights.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: \(n\) is the i.i.d. sample size.

symbols.name: X_sample
symbols.def: \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) are i.i.d. draws from \(P\).

symbols.name: C_hat
symbols.def: For \(n\ge R\), \(\widehat C_{\le R}\) is the vector of multivariate \(k\)-statistics through order \(R\); for \(n<R\), \(\widehat C_{\le R}=\bot\).

symbols.name: V_P
symbols.def: For laws \(P\) with finite moments through order \(2R\), \(V_P=\operatorname{avar}_P\{\sqrt n(\widehat C_{\le R}-C_{\le R})\}\) is the finite asymptotic covariance on the domain \(n\ge R\).

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: \(\alpha\) is the nominal error probability.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: \(M\) is a known coordinatewise envelope for the observed vector \(X\).

symbols.name: M_ell_bd
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{bd}}_{\ell,M}\) is the subclass of \(\mathcal M_{\ell}\) whose observed vector satisfies \(\lVert X\rVert_{\infty}\le M\) almost surely.

symbols.name: A_multi_R
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_R=\{\nu\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^3:1\le|\nu|\le R\}\).

symbols.name: p_R
symbols.def: \(p_R=|\mathcal A_R|=\binom{R+3}{3}-1\).

symbols.name: mu_R
symbols.def: \(\mu_R=(\mathbb E_P[X^{\nu}])_{\nu\in\mathcal A_R}\).

symbols.name: mu_hat_R
symbols.def: \(\widehat\mu_R=(n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^n (X^{(s)})^{\nu})_{\nu\in\mathcal A_R}\).

symbols.name: Kappa_R
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K_R\) is the standard multivariate moment-to-cumulant polynomial map through order \(R\).

symbols.name: rho_n
symbols.def: \(\rho_n=\max\{1,M\}^{R}\sqrt{2\log(2p_R/\alpha)/n}\).

symbols.name: Lambda_R_M
symbols.def: \(\Lambda_{R,M}=\sup_{\lVert m\rVert_{\infty}\le2\max\{1,M\}^{R}}\lVert D\mathcal K_R(m)\rVert_{\infty\to\infty}\) is finite because a polynomial derivative is continuous on this nonempty compact box, and is explicitly computable for fixed \(R\).

symbols.name: Q_n
symbols.def: \(Q_n=\{\zeta:\exists m\in\mathbb R^{p_R},\ \lVert m-\widehat\mu_R\rVert_{\infty}\le\rho_n,\ \zeta=\mathcal K_R(m)\}\) is the finite quantified-real image of the empirical raw-moment box.

symbols.name: J_n
symbols.def: \(\mathcal J_n=Q_n\cap\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\) is the total legal-moment intersection; it is allowed to be empty.

symbols.name: B_ell_R
symbols.def: For \(\zeta\in\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), \(\mathcal B_{\ell,R}(\zeta)=\{b:\exists\theta\in\Theta_{\ell,R},\ \Phi_{\ell,R}(\theta)=\zeta,\ \beta(\theta)=b\}\), with membership decided by the finite atomic quantified-real presentation of \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\).

symbols.name: omega_ell_R
symbols.def: For \(\delta\ge0\) and \(\zeta\in\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), \(\omega_{\ell,R}(\delta;\zeta)=\operatorname{diam}\bigcup\{\mathcal B_{\ell,R}(\zeta'):\zeta'\in\mathcal O_{\ell,R},\ \lVert\zeta'-\zeta\rVert_{\infty}\le\delta\}\in[0,\infty]\); the union is nonempty because it contains \(\mathcal B_{\ell,R}(\zeta)\).

symbols.name: I_n
symbols.def: \(I_n=\bigcup_{\zeta\in\mathcal J_n}\mathcal B_{\ell,R}(\zeta)\) is a total finite quantified-real projection, with \(I_n=\varnothing\) when \(\mathcal J_n=\varnothing\).

symbols.name: eta_n_chi
symbols.def: For \(\chi\in\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,R}\), \(\eta_{n,\chi}=\inf_{\zeta\in\mathcal J_n}|\Delta_{\chi}(\zeta)|/(1+|\Delta_{\chi}(\zeta)|)\) when \(\mathcal J_n\ne\varnothing\), and \(\eta_{n,\chi}=0\) when \(\mathcal J_n=\varnothing\).

symbols.name: s_n_chi
symbols.def: For \(n\ge R\), \(s_{n,\chi}=|\Delta_{\chi}(\widehat C_{\le R})|/(1+|\Delta_{\chi}(\widehat C_{\le R})|)\); for \(n<R\), set \(s_{n,\chi}=0\).

symbols.name: chi_n
symbols.def: If \(n\ge R\) and \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,R}\ne\varnothing\), then \(\chi_n\) is the first maximizer of \(s_{n,\chi}\) in the fixed \(d\)-then-lexicographic order; if either condition fails, \(\chi_n=\bot\).

symbols.name: chi_star
symbols.def: If \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,R}\ne\varnothing\), then \(\chi_{\star}\) is the first maximizer of \(|\Delta_{\chi}(C_{\le R})|/(1+|\Delta_{\chi}(C_{\le R})|)\) in the fixed order; if the atlas is empty, \(\chi_{\star}=\bot\).

symbols.name: d_n
symbols.def: \(d_n=d_{\chi_n}\) when \(\chi_n\ne\bot\), and \(d_n=\bot\) otherwise.

symbols.name: eta_n
symbols.def: \(\eta_n=\eta_{n,\chi_n}\) when \(\chi_n\ne\bot\), and \(\eta_n=0\) when \(\chi_n=\bot\); this is the total sample-computable separation for the deterministic selector.

symbols.name: beta_hat
symbols.def: If \(\chi_n\ne\bot\) and \(\widehat C_{\le R}\in\mathcal U_{\chi_n}\), then \(\widehat\beta_n=g_{\chi_n}(\widehat C_{\le R})\); otherwise \(\widehat\beta_n=\bot\).

assumptions.condition: \[Z=\sum_{i\in I_{\ell}}a_iL_i+\varepsilon_Z,\qquad T=\gamma Z+\sum_{i\in I_{\ell}}b_iL_i+\varepsilon_T,\qquad Y=\beta T+\sum_{i\in I_{\ell}}c_iL_i+\varepsilon_Y.\]

standard.name: Bounded observed-data envelope for simultaneous Hoeffding concentration

definitions.name: Legal realizable truncated-moment domain
definitions.construction: \[\Theta_{\ell,R}=\left\{(\gamma,\beta,u,v,m^{S}):\begin{array}{l}\gamma\prod_{i\in I_{\ell}}(u_i-\gamma)(v_i-\beta u_i)\ne0,\ \text{and for every }j\in J_{\ell}\text{ there exist }(w^{S}_{j,k},x^{S}_{j,k})_{k\in K_R}\text{ such that}\\ w^{S}_{j,k}\ge0,\ \sum_kw^{S}_{j,k}=1,\ \sum_kw^{S}_{j,k}x^{S}_{j,k}=0,\ m^{S}_{j,r}=\sum_kw^{S}_{j,k}(x^{S}_{j,k})^r\ (0\le r\le R),\ m^{S}_{j,2}>0\end{array}\right\},\qquad a_i=1,\ b_i=u_i-\gamma,\ c_i=v_i-\beta u_i.\]

definitions.name: Effect-identifying cumulant depth
Rational recovery atlas and exceptional polynomial
definitions.construction: Enumerate \(d\) increasingly, then row minors \(J\), kernel pivots \(p\), and denominator candidates \(k\) lexicographically. Each record \(\chi=(d,J,p,k)\) defines a polynomial \(\Delta_{\chi}\) on the full cumulant space and the semialgebraic domain \(\mathcal U_{\chi}=\{\Delta_{\chi}\ne0\}\). Row reduction defines \(f_{\chi}\) and the contraction ratio on \(\mathcal U_{\chi}\); set \(g_{\chi}=\bot\) on its complement. Retain \(\chi\) in \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,R}\) exactly when \(\mathcal U_{\chi}\cap\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\ne\varnothing\) and quantified real elimination verifies \(g_{\chi}(\Phi_{\ell,R}(\theta))=\beta(\theta)\) throughout that legal domain. The construction always terminates and may return the empty atlas.

definitions.name: Saturated real-fiber handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathfrak H_{\ell}\): form the complete two-representation incidence ideal with common \(C_{\le R}\), saturate by the graph and regular-chart factors, project to \((\beta,\beta')\), and impose finitely atomic positive truncated-moment constraints on every surviving real component.

definitions.name: Saturated legal-fiber certificate and atomic charts
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathfrak H_{1,3}\) to the complete modified map used by Tramontano et al.: reproduce its elimination basis and beta quadratic over \(\mathcal D_{1,3}\), then adjoin \(\mathcal R^{\mathrm{legal}}_{1,3}\) and return an exact Stengle Positivstellensatz or equivalent real-quantifier-elimination certificate that the additional beta factor has no legal lift on \(s_{1,3}\ne0\). List the rational three-atom formulas, the nonempty semialgebraic boxes \(\mathcal W_3\) and \(\mathcal W_2\), and define \(\Psi_3,\Psi_2^{+},\Psi_2^{-}\) to return \(\bot\) outside those boxes.

definitions.name: Simultaneous polynomial-moment confidence fiber
definitions.construction: For \(\zeta\in\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), set \(\mathcal B_{\ell,R}(\zeta)=\{b:\exists\theta\in\Theta_{\ell,R},\ \Phi_{\ell,R}(\theta)=\zeta,\ \beta(\theta)=b\}\). Set \(\mathcal J_n=Q_n\cap\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\) and \(I_n=\bigcup_{\zeta\in\mathcal J_n}\mathcal B_{\ell,R}(\zeta)\), with the standard empty-union convention \(I_n=\varnothing\) when \(\mathcal J_n=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Deterministic established-chart selector
definitions.construction: If \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,R}=\varnothing\), set \(\chi_n=\chi_{\star}=d_n=\bot\). For a nonempty atlas, apply the population maximization and fixed tie-break at \(C_{\le R}\) to define \(\chi_{\star}\). If additionally \(n\ge R\), compute \(s_{n,\chi}=|\Delta_{\chi}(\widehat C_{\le R})|/(1+|\Delta_{\chi}(\widehat C_{\le R})|)\), take the first maximizer as \(\chi_n\), and set \(d_n=d_{\chi_n}\); if \(n<R\), set \(\chi_n=d_n=\bot\).

definitions.name: Separated-chart estimator
definitions.construction: If \(\chi_n\ne\bot\) and \(\widehat C_{\le R}\in\mathcal U_{\chi_n}\), set \(\widehat\beta_n=g_{\chi_n}(\widehat C_{\le R})\); otherwise set \(\widehat\beta_n=\bot\).

definitions.name: Selected-chart confidence-region separation
definitions.construction: If \(\chi_n=\bot\) or \(\mathcal J_n=\varnothing\), set \(\eta_n=0\). Otherwise compute \(\eta_{n,\chi_n}=\inf_{\zeta\in\mathcal J_n}|\Delta_{\chi_n}(\zeta)|/(1+|\Delta_{\chi_n}(\zeta)|)\) by quantified real algebra and set \(\eta_n=\eta_{n,\chi_n}\).

statements.statement: For every \(R\ge d+2\) and every \(\zeta\in\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), the complete proxy-anchored map satisfies \(A_{R,d}=B_{R,d}E_d\) in each \(\theta\in F_{\ell,R}(\zeta)\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{R,d})=\ell+1<N_d\), then every \(f\in\ker A_{R,d}\) annihilates all normalized source columns \(p_0,\ldots,p_{\ell}\) in every member of that nonempty legal fiber.
statements.justification: The factorization uses all ternary compatibility equations and isolates the target without reconstructing the latent loading list.
statements.gap: Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton recover bivariate loading roots; their construction does not state this complete-tensor kernel identity.
statements.consumer: The identity supplies the lower-order recovery primitive for CEId-from-Moments.

statements.statement: For every \(\ell\ge1\), \(\mathcal O_{\ell,U_{\ell}}\ne\varnothing\), the terminating construction returns a nonempty finite atlas \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,U_{\ell}}\), and \(\bigcup_{\chi\in\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,U_{\ell}}}(\mathcal U_{\chi}\cap\mathcal O_{\ell,U_{\ell}})\) contains a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of the legal image. For every \(\zeta\) in that union and every atlas chart \(\chi\) covering \(\zeta\), \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{U_{\ell},d_{\chi}})=\ell+1\), \(g_{\chi}(\zeta)\in\mathbb R\), and \(g_{\chi}(\zeta)=\beta(\theta)\) for all \(\theta\in F_{\ell,U_{\ell}}(\zeta)\). For every legal \(\zeta\) outside that union all atlas charts return \(\bot\), so the simultaneous vanishing of the listed discriminants is an explicit failure certificate, not a point estimate. Consequently \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\) and \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\le U_{\ell}<k(\ell)=(\ell+2)+\lceil(-3+\sqrt{8\ell+17})/2\rceil\).
statements.justification: This is the constructive strict improvement over the published sufficient depth and provides an observable instability certificate.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorems 3.4--3.5, guarantee identification only through the larger pairwise-recovery order \(k(\ell)\).
statements.consumer: CEId-from-Moments can lower its required empirical moment order and return \(\bot\) with the simultaneous-discriminant certificate whenever no recovery chart covers the observed cumulants.

statements.statement: For \(\ell=1\), \(r_{\beta}(1)=3\). On a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{1,3}\), if \(M_3\) has rank two and \(f\ne0\) spans its kernel with \(\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,T)\ne0\), then the displayed ratio is defined and every nonempty legal fiber satisfies \(\beta=\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,Y)/\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,T)\). Tramontano et al., Theorem 3.6, parameterizes the complete modified map \((\beta,\Phi_{1,3})\) and computes its vanishing ideal; the resulting quadratic is reproduced over the full algebraic relaxation \(\mathcal D_{1,3}\). Its additional algebraic beta factor has no lift satisfying \(\mathcal R^{\mathrm{legal}}_{1,3}\): an exact real-infeasibility certificate enforces positive diagonal order-two source variances and one centered representing law for each order-two--three source tuple. The explicitly displayed domain \(\mathcal W_3\) is nonempty, and \(\Psi_3(t)\in\Theta_{1,3}\) for every \(t\in\mathcal W_3\), while \(\Psi_3(t)=\bot\) outside that domain. The explicitly displayed domain \(\mathcal W_2\) is nonempty, and for every \(t\in\mathcal W_2\), \(\Psi_2^{+}(t),\Psi_2^{-}(t)\in\Theta_{1,2}\) are legal independent centered non-Gaussian three-atom source realizations with equal covariance tuples and unequal effects; their common covariance tuples contain a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{1,2}\).
statements.justification: The first exact case both validates the annihilator and prevents algebraic polynomial degree from being mistaken for legal statistical multiplicity.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorem 3.6, correctly computes the vanishing ideal of the complete modified algebraic map but treats diagonal cumulant coordinates algebraically; the new result audits the missing real source-moment domain and shows that polynomial degree two does not furnish a second legal preimage.
statements.consumer: The one-latent branch of CEId-from-Moments can use third rather than fourth cumulants.

statements.statement: If \(\binom{R+2}{2}\le\ell+3\), then there is a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), contained in the image of legal finite-support parameter points, such that every \(\zeta\) in that subset has a curve in the nonempty fiber \(F_{\ell,R}(\zeta)\) along which \(\beta\) varies. Consequently \(L_{\ell}\le r_{\beta}(\ell)\le U_{\ell}\) and \(r_{\beta}(\ell)/\sqrt{2\ell}\to1\).
statements.justification: The lower bound is robust on a legal moment chart rather than resting on one algebraic or nonreal witness.
statements.gap: Neither the anchor nor generic dimension counting constructs real independent-source unequal-effect fibers on an open legal region.
statements.consumer: The asymptotic square-root frontier determines how the minimum data moment order scales with latent complexity.

statements.statement: For \(\ell=3\), \(r_{\beta}(3)=4\): on a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{3,3}\), the augmented Jacobian \(D(\Phi_{3,3},\beta)\) has rank strictly larger than \(D\Phi_{3,3}\) along preimages in \(\Theta_{3,3}\) and \(\beta\) varies within every legal fiber. At order four, \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{3,4}\ne\varnothing\), and the union of its domains \(\mathcal U_{\chi}\cap\mathcal O_{3,4}\) contains a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset; on this union every covering chart returns the common legal-fiber effect, and outside all chart domains every recovery map returns \(\bot\). Consequently, the Tramontano--Kivva--Salehkaleybar--Kiyavash--Drton workflow specialized to three latent confounders can replace its sufficient input \(C_{\le k(3)}=C_{\le7}\) by \(C_{\le4}\) on that regular legal image, while no procedure using only \(C_{\le3}\) can report a generically identified point effect on the stated open lower-fiber locus.
statements.justification: The exact three-latent case converts a fiber calculation into a seven-to-four reduction in required empirical cumulant order and a sharp order-three nonidentification decision.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorems 3.4--3.5, specialize to the sufficient order \(k(3)=7\) and do not show either order-four sufficiency from the complete tensor or generic failure at order three.
statements.consumer: For \(\ell=3\), CEId-from-Moments can stop after estimating \(C_{\le4}\) instead of \(C_{\le7}\); if only \(C_{\le3}\) is available on the open lower-fiber locus, it must return nonidentification rather than a selected point estimate.

statements.statement: Determine the finite value of \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\) exactly for every \(\ell\ge1\). Using \(\mathfrak H_{\ell}\), prove that for every \(R\ge r_{\beta}(\ell)\) the terminating atlas is nonempty and its domains cover a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}=\Phi_{\ell,R}(\Theta_{\ell,R})\), where every covering chart returns \(\beta\) and all uncovered legal inputs return the common failure value \(\bot\). For every \(2\le R<r_{\beta}(\ell)\), construct a Zariski-dense relatively open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\) whose nonempty legal fibers contain independent finite-support unequal-\(\beta\) twins. The mandatory first decision is the complete saturated \(\ell=2,R=3\) projection \(\{\beta(\theta):\theta\in F_{2,3}(\zeta)\}\) using the finite atomic quantified-real constraints of \(\Theta_{2,3}\) on a relatively open legal image chart; abandon the global converse architecture if no open legal-twin chamber exists there.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it closes both the sufficiency and legal-real necessity sides of the minimum-depth problem.
statements.gap: The closest paper supplies only \(k(\ell)\)-order sufficiency and a disputed one-latent lower claim; no exact all-\(\ell\) fiber frontier is known.
statements.consumer: The result fixes the minimum moment order and the failure certificate used by the companion estimator.

statements.statement: In the standard no-latent special case \(\ell=0\), \(\gamma=\operatorname{Cov}(Z,T)/\operatorname{Var}(Z)\) and \(\beta=\{\operatorname{Cov}(T,Y)-\gamma\operatorname{Cov}(Z,Y)\}/\{\operatorname{Var}(T)-\gamma\operatorname{Cov}(Z,T)\}\) whenever the denominator is nonzero.
statements.justification: The frontier must reduce to ordinary residualized linear identification when latent confounding is absent.
statements.gap: This is a required sanity reduction, not a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It checks normalization and implementation against the familiar covariance formula.

statements.justification: The minimal-order population map becomes a usable estimator with an explicit instability boundary.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al. prove plug-in consistency but do not give this chart-specific limit law and sandwich variance.
statements.consumer: Applied users obtain standard errors whenever the reported chart discriminant is separated from zero.

sampling_model.design: Observational i.i.d. sampling from one fixed member of \(\mathcal M_{\ell}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention target is the structural edge coefficient \(\beta\) on \(T\to Y\); treatment is not randomized.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used; regular inference is reported only when the deterministic selector returns an established chart whose discriminant is nonzero, while confidence-fiber inversion remains total at chart collisions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate all entries of \(C_{\le R}\) by multivariate \(k\)-statistics. The fixed degree-then-lexicographic selector returns \(\chi_n,d_n,\widehat\beta_n\) only on their declared established-chart domain and returns \(\bot\) otherwise. For collision-robust inversion, compute \(\widehat\mu_R\), \(\rho_n\), \(Q_n\), the possibly empty legal intersection \(\mathcal J_n\), the total projected set \(I_n\), and \(\eta_n\) from the finite atomic quantified-real presentation of \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\).

estimand_functional: \(g_{\chi}(C_{\le R})=\beta=C_{d_{\chi}+2}[f_{\chi},T,Y]/C_{d_{\chi}+2}[f_{\chi},T,T]\) for \(\chi\in\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,R}\) and \(C_{\le R}\in\mathcal U_{\chi}\); otherwise \(g_{\chi}(C_{\le R})=\bot\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 3.4--3.5 identify the proxy-model effect from cumulants through \(k(\ell)\).
Specializing Theorems 3.4--3.5 to three latent confounders gives the sufficient input order \(k(3)=7\).
Theorem 3.6 claims order-three nonidentification for \(\ell=1\) after computing the vanishing ideal of the complete modified map and obtaining a quadratic in the effect coordinate.
Theorem 4 gives a degree-\(\ell+1\) bivariate loading polynomial whose coefficients use higher-order cumulants.
Propositions 3--4 give elimination-ideal criteria for generic identifiability of a target coordinate.
The paper gives cross-moment effect formulas in a one-confounder proxy setting and a Gaussian impossibility result.
Theorem 3.8 characterizes full-law effect identifiability in lvLiNGAM through overcomplete ICA.
Theorems 1.5 and 1.9 characterize full-distribution overcomplete-ICA mixing identifiability.
The paper develops tests for algebraic cumulant-rank constraints using incomplete \(U\)-statistics.
The paper constructs identification- and singularity-robust confidence sets for nonlinear moment-condition models.
The paper projects inverted causal-model tests to retain structural uncertainty.
The paper identifies causal effects from a single proxy under a known proxy mechanism.

tldr: Higher-order cumulants identify the treatment effect in a single-proxy latent-confounded LiNGAM, but the published order \(k(\ell)\) is only sufficient. The project characterizes the exact least depth \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\) over nonempty fibers on relatively Zariski-open subsets of the explicitly quantified legal observable image, combining a terminating proxy-anchored annihilator atlas above the frontier with open sets of real finite-support unequal-effect twins below it. The exact three-latent result changes the Tramontano et al. workflow from cumulants through \(k(3)=7\) to the sharp order four and requires a nonidentification report at order three on the open lower-fiber locus. Their one-latent proof correctly computes the vanishing ideal of the complete modified order-three map, but its quadratic algebraic projection does not enforce positive source variances and simultaneous centered truncated-moment realizability; the correction supplies an exact real-feasibility certificate and domain-indexed three-atom charts. The all-\(\ell\) kernel retains the mandatory complete \(\ell=2,R=3\) decision. Every scalar recovery and chart-selection construction is totalized by the common value \(\bot\) outside its proved domain; an established separated chart yields the \(k\)-statistic limit, while a total, possibly empty confidence-fiber projection gives uniform coverage, an \(n^{-1/2}\) radius, and collision-aware diameter bounds.

project_justification.gap: The nearest paper proves identification from pairwise cumulant roots through \(k(\ell)\) and claims a one-latent order-three lower result; it does not determine the minimum information depth of the complete ternary law, and its algebraic projection argument does not restrict the extra root to realizable centered source moments with positive variances.
project_justification.niche: The graph creates a distinguished proxy-zero pair of noise columns, so homogeneous forms annihilating only the sources entering \(Z\) can identify \(\beta\) before the entire overcomplete mixing matrix is recoverable.
project_justification.fill: The paper will provide the exact finite-\(\ell\) depth on the finite-atomic quantified-real observable image, a finite established rational atlas with explicit nonvanishing domains and a common failure output off those domains, legal-real converse fibers at all lower orders, an auditable real-infeasibility certificate for the additional one-latent algebraic root, and inference that switches from a proved separated Wald chart to total confidence-fiber inversion at the discriminant. At \(\ell=3\), the exact theorem replaces the published sufficient input \(C_{\le7}\) by the sharp \(C_{\le4}\) requirement and rules out point identification from \(C_{\le3}\) on the stated open locus.

related_work: Tramontano et al. (2025, Theorems 3.4--3.5) recover pairwise loading-root lists through \(k(\ell)\) and align them by source cumulants; Theorem 2 is a strict tightening because its complete-tensor contraction identifies on the covered relatively Zariski-open part of the same legal observable image at \(U_{\ell}<k(\ell)\), with an explicit failure output elsewhere. At \(\ell=3\), their sufficient workflow uses \(k(3)=7\), whereas Theorem 5 proves that order four is both sufficient and minimal on the stated generic legal loci; this removes orders five through seven from the workflow and changes the order-three output from a selected point to nonidentification. The proof of their Theorem 3.6 parameterizes the complete modified order-three cumulant map and computes its vanishing ideal; Theorem 3 accepts that algebraic calculation and isolates the domain gap: a second root of the projected quadratic must lift to a real graph point whose diagonal order-two cumulants are positive variances and whose order-two--three coordinates have a common centered representing law. The exact real-infeasibility certificate excludes only the additional branch under these legal restrictions and supplies explicitly domain-indexed positive three-atom charts for the retained branch and covariance twins. Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024, Theorem 4) supplies higher-cumulant rank matrices and annihilating polynomials for bivariate latent LiNGAM, but does not classify the simultaneous ternary beta projection. Garcia-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010, Propositions 3--4) supplies the target-elimination framework adapted by the exact-frontier handle. Tramontano et al. (2024, Theorem 3.8) and Wang and Seigal (2026, Theorems 1.5 and 1.9) concern full-distribution effect or mixing identification, leaving finite truncation depth open. Kivva, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2023) is the scalar cross-moment precursor. Schkoda and Drton (2025), Andrews and Guggenberger (2019), and Strieder et al. (2021) inform, respectively, cumulant-rank testing, singular moment inference, and projected causal-model inversion. Vollmer, Pfister, and Weichwald (2026) identify effects with a single proxy under a known proxy mechanism and therefore do not subsume the unknown-mechanism non-Gaussian graph studied here.
technical_internal_limitation: The contraction discriminant is initially a certificate-failure locus, not yet the true nonidentification locus. Accordingly, every chart-specific scalar construction returns \(\bot\) when its atlas is empty, its pivot or denominator vanishes, or its input lies outside the chart domain; no value on that failure locus is interpreted as an effect. The exact \(\ell=2,R=3\) real beta projection under the quantified finite-atomic source-moment constraints is the mandatory early decision. Complex fiber degree, Jacobian rank, failure of one annihilator, an unrestricted diagonal-cumulant solution, and a single finite-support witness are each insufficient for the global converse. The order-three algebraic image closure permits diagonal cumulant coordinates that need not be positive-variance centered source moments; polynomial degree alone therefore does not count legal preimages. Uniform confidence-fiber coverage uses the explicit observed-data envelope \(\lVert X\rVert_{\infty}\le M\); no observed bound is inferred from bounded latent sources or bounded disturbances with unrestricted structural coefficients. Off the simultaneous moment-coverage event the legal intersection and projected set may be empty and are reported as such. At an exact collision, honest coverage need not imply singleton contraction, and the limiting diameter is the legal-fiber modulus rather than a Wald rate.
honest_scope: The full-fiber contraction identity, improved upper depth, one- and three-latent exact cases, and weight-saturation lower region are theorem obligations supported by symbolic presolve but remain to be proved independently. The three-latent obligation has the independent operational content that \(C_{\le4}\), rather than the published sufficient \(C_{\le7}\), is the sharp generic input and that \(C_{\le3}\) cannot support a point-effect report on the open lower-fiber locus. The one-latent obligation reproduces the published complete modified-map vanishing ideal and then audits the additional quadratic branch only against the positive-variance, centered finite-atomic truncated-moment domain; it does not allege that the published elimination omitted cumulant equations. The exact finite-\(\ell\) frontier and global real-feasible lower-fiber theorem are the first-class open content, with the complete \(\ell=2,R=3\) legal beta projection under the same quantified-real domain as the mandatory early kill test. Uniform inference is confined to an observed-data envelope class. Wald output exists only on a proved established-chart domain and is \(\bot\) otherwise; confidence-fiber inversion is total, may return the empty set off coverage, and remains set-valued at unidentified collisions. When \(\ell=0\), the construction reduces to the standard covariance residualization formula. The bivariate causal-direction minimal-order frontier is a different object: it orients an arrow from two observed variables, whereas this project fixes the proxy graph and identifies one interventional coefficient from the complete trivariate cumulant map.

seed_details.title: Exact cumulant-depth frontier for the proxy effect
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace pairwise loading-root recovery and signature matching in Theorems 3.4--3.5 by a kernel of the complete proxy-anchored ternary cumulant contraction.
seed_details.destination_search: A search for the exact target--method pair \(\{\)single proxy, graph-constrained complete ternary cumulant fiber, least order for \(\beta\)\(\}\) found the ICML sufficient bound and bivariate cumulant papers, but no exact finite-depth theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Tramontano et al. because their \(k(\ell)\)-order algorithm already identifies \(\beta\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Their construction proves sufficiency at \(k(\ell)\); it neither minimizes the complete ternary cumulant order nor supplies legal real unequal-effect fibers below it, and the complete-tensor contraction already lowers the order for \(\ell=1,2\).

seed_details.title: The complete \(\ell=2,R=3\) beta-fiber decision
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain all order-two and order-three ternary cumulants, eliminate two graph-compatible representations simultaneously, and decide every projected beta branch against the quantified finite-atomic source-moment domain.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for saturated \(\ell=2\) proxy-LiNGAM elimination and real moment-feasible third-cumulant fibers returned no paper beyond the sufficient-order construction.
seed_details.red_team: A square Jacobian at \(R=3\) makes generic identification routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: A full-rank parameter-to-moment Jacobian gives local finite fibers but does not prove that their \(\beta\)-projection is a singleton or that other real legal branches are absent.

seed_details.title: Separated-chart limits and collision-robust confidence fibers
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After replacing pairwise roots by a finite established full-tensor atlas, prove stability of the fixed score-and-tie-break selector away from its discriminants and invert simultaneous polynomial moment regions at collisions.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found consistency for the proxy estimator, rank-constraint tests, and general singularity-robust GMM, but no confidence procedure for the beta projection of this simultaneous cumulant fiber.
seed_details.red_team: This is a direct delta-method corollary of any rational identifying formula.
seed_details.rebuttal: The regular-chart limit requires a stable selector over already established identifying charts, while uniform coverage through root collisions requires set-valued inversion over legal structural fibers and cannot be obtained by differentiating a selected root.

seed_details.title: Legal-real audit of the published one-latent quadratic
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Reproduce the complete modified-map vanishing ideal and then test each factor of its degree-two beta relation against positive source variances and simultaneous centered finite-atomic truncated-moment realizability.
seed_details.destination_search: No public correction or independent real-moment-domain audit of Theorem 3.6 was located.
seed_details.red_team: A correction of one lower-bound example is too narrow for a paper.
seed_details.rebuttal: The correction changes the exact answer to \(r_{\beta}(1)=3\), but it is retained as a theorem and diagnostic inside the broader all-\(\ell\) frontier rather than as the stand-alone kernel.

seed_details.title: Source-signature-dependent effect depth
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace generic equality of source signatures in the matching argument by a rank condition on the actually nonzero cumulant-order signature matrix.
seed_details.destination_search: Full-distribution overcomplete ICA gives an if-and-only-if mixing criterion, but the search found no finite-order, source-pattern-dependent frontier for this causal coefficient.
seed_details.red_team: Vanishing odd cumulants are merely nongeneric exceptions already excluded by the anchor.
seed_details.rebuttal: Symmetric and initially moment-matched sources are scientifically common, and a pattern-dependent theorem would characterize rather than discard the entire collision strata; nevertheless it broadens the present exact-generic kernel and is deferred.

seed_details.title: Exact exceptional atlas for rational beta recovery
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compute the radical saturated target-identification ideal and distinguish the union of chart-denominator failures from the true nonidentification locus.
seed_details.destination_search: Algebraic-identification frameworks classify generic identifiability, but no located work computes this proxy graph's beta atlas.
seed_details.red_team: An exceptional set is bookkeeping once one rational formula is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: A certificate-failure locus can strictly exceed the nonidentification locus, so equality requires a new fiber theorem; the object is valuable but narrower than the depth frontier.

seed_details.title: Effect depth versus full mixing depth
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project the finite-cumulant mixing fiber to \(\beta\) before imposing uniqueness up to column scaling and permutation.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found full-distribution mixing identifiability and finite-order loading recovery, but no derived gap between the least order for a graph coefficient and the least order for the whole mixing matrix.
seed_details.red_team: Effect identification is automatically equivalent to mixing-matrix identification in LiNGAM.
seed_details.rebuttal: The distinguished treatment-noise column yields a contraction ratio that can be constant while nuisance source decompositions remain nonunique, so the two depths need not coincide.

seed_details.title: Data-adaptive cumulant-order selection with honest coverage
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Use rank-minor tests to choose the first certified contraction chart and account for that selection in a simultaneous confidence-fiber inversion.
seed_details.destination_search: No proxy-LiNGAM procedure was found that selects cumulant order while retaining coverage after selection.
seed_details.red_team: Bonferroni over finitely many moment orders makes the result immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Bonferroni controls moment-region coverage, but useful stopping and beta-set contraction near singular strata require a nontrivial nested-fiber analysis; this is better treated after the population frontier is known.

seed_details.title: Sample-size cost of the minimum identifying cumulant order
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Translate the exact algebraic order into a tail-index-dependent minimax experiment before applying empirical cumulants.
seed_details.destination_search: No minimax rate theorem was found for this proxy effect as the number of confounders and usable moment order grow.
seed_details.red_team: Without a fixed tail class the rate question is undefined, and imposing one would change the accepted model.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the present brief; this seed is rejected rather than padded with an oracle tail assumption.

seed_details.selection_reason: The exact-depth seed has the strongest direct contradiction and constructive upper-bound evidence, contains the \(\ell=2,R=3\) decision as a decisive bounded kill test, and gives the inference seed a well-defined minimal moment vector.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is not a bare application of cumulants or do-calculus: it asks for a necessary-and-sufficient order frontier, a terminating recovery atlas, and generic legal-real converse fibers over an explicitly quantified realizable truncated-moment image. The lower result is required on a relatively open legal moment region, not at one hand-tuned law. The inference rung is attached to the algebraic frontier and does not replace it.

novelty_justification: The closest result, Tramontano et al. (2025, Theorems 3.4--3.5), identifies \(\beta\) using cumulants through \(k(\ell)\) by recovering three bivariate root lists and matching source signatures. The proposed complete-tensor annihilator instead targets \(\beta\) without reconstructing those lists and yields a strictly smaller general upper order \(U_{\ell}\). The exact \(\ell=3\) classification sharpens their specialized sufficient order \(k(3)=7\) to the necessary-and-sufficient order four and establishes generic nonidentification at order three. For \(\ell=1\), their Theorem 3.6 correctly obtains a quadratic from the vanishing ideal of the complete modified order-three map, whereas the new classification asks whether both algebraic roots lift to the explicitly defined real truncated-moment domain and certifies that the additional factor does not; this yields \(r_{\beta}(1)=3\) without disputing the published ideal computation. Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024, Theorem 4) supplies the bivariate polynomial machinery but neither exploits simultaneous ternary compatibility nor characterizes target-coordinate fibers. The novel kernel is the exact finite-\(\ell\) necessary-and-sufficient depth with legal real lower fibers, not merely the already-derived improved upper bound.
